Ivy (CSM): Heads-up: Solara Health go-live next Monday. They asked for a short SLO packet (uptime, p95 latency) + a concrete credit worked example for finance. Can SRE/Eng help pull numbers and a plain-language calc?
Derek (SRE): Yep. Contract lists 99.5% monthly availability and p95 < 300ms per route. I'll pull 30d availability and flag any days < 99.3%.
Rao (Eng): I'll export route-level p95 and per-region split. Also include a note about automatic fallback routing that can add ~30-50ms tail.
Ivy (CSM): Legal wants downtime defined as any continuous interval >=5 minutes where availability < target. p95 measured per UTC day per route.
Sofia (Enablement): I can draft the one-pager + FAQ. Will include a worked example showing math for a 30-day billing period where observed availability = 99.2%.
Derek (SRE): Simple example I'll drop in doc: 30 days = 43,200 minutes. Allowed downtime at 99.5% = 216 minutes. Observed downtime at 99.2% = 345.6 minutes. Minutes below target = 129.6. Credit% = 129.6 / 43,200 ≈ 0.3% of monthly bill (subject to contractual cap).
Rao (Eng): I'll mark traces where fallback occurred so customers can see them in the console. We'll add JSON exports and a p95 histogram screenshot.
ops-bot: KB link added: https://console.redwood.com/kb/latency-warmup (auto)
Ivy (CSM): Timeline: can we have raw exports today and a draft one-pager by tomorrow morning? Customer briefing Wed afternoon.
Derek (SRE): I'll upload CSV + query to the onboarding evidence folder today and flag any anomalies >0.2% from baseline.
Sofia (Enablement): Drafting slides now: 1 slide uptime, 1 slide latency, 1 slide credit worked example, 1 FAQ.
Ivy (CSM): Thanks all — I'll assemble and send the customer packet once artifacts are in the folder.
